text:
Alisha: Heads-up — a customer asked for 'multiple tool calls inside one chat turn' with concurrent execution, per-call timeouts, and a retry budget. Want to surface this for roadmap prioritization.
Matt: Which customer and scale? is this enterprise-only?
Alisha: Strategic enterprise POC (finance) but they said it's a blocking feature for GA. They need: up to 8 parallel external invocations, ability to surface partial responses as they arrive, and control over ordering for some steps.
Jordan: Quick API thought: we should offer explicit modes rather than implicit concurrency. Proposal: mode: "parallel_best_effort" | "sequenced" | "transactional". Add per-invoke opts like `timeout_ms`, `retry_budget`, and `idempotency_key`. Eg:
```json
{
  "mode": "parallel_best_effort",
  "invocations": [ { "tool": "price_fetch", "timeout_ms": 500, "retry_budget": 1 }, ... ]
}
```
Sara: Cost/SLA notes: paralleling 8 calls per chat turn multiplies egress and tokenization costs. Need to define service-level latency targets (p90/p99) for the whole turn when customer enables parallel mode. Also: caching/dedup will matter across concurrent calls.
Liz: Prioritization lens: criteria to decide roadmap slot — #customers impacted, security/SOC2 concerns (external calls), engineering effort, and whether we can reuse existing retry/timeout primitives. Launch criteria suggestion: 1) clear API contract docs + SDK examples, 2) perf tests hitting p95 latency budget, 3) observability (per-invoke tracing), 4) canary with one enterprise POC.
Alisha: For MVP scope I suggest: support `parallel_best_effort` with a configurable `max_concurrency` (default 4), per-invoke `timeout_ms`, and `retry_budget`. No transactional semantics or automatic rollback in MVP. Partial-response streaming should be supported (stream each tool result as it completes).
Matt: For retries: must require explicit idempotency for any non-idempotent tool. We should surface a warning if retry_budget > 0 and tool not idempotent. Also: what about ordering guarantees for when caller wants deterministic order?
Jordan: Add optional `ordering_hint` per invocation (integer). When set, runtime will try to emit results in that order (best-effort) — but document it's not a strict serial execution unless mode=="sequenced".
Sara: Observability: we need per-invocation logs, bytes/cost attribution, and a way to correlate all invocations to a single chat turn (trace_id). This will be required for billing reconciliation and debugging.
Liz: Non-goals for MVP: distributed transactions, long lived saga orchestration, and automatic cross-tool compensation. We can capture those in roadmap later.
Alisha: Action items: 1) Jordan + Matt draft an RFC with API samples and SDK surface, 2) Sara to write perf/cost acceptance tests, 3) Liz to map customer POCs and gating criteria, 4) I'll own release acceptance and enterprise rollout plan. Target milestone: Q3 beta.
Matt: SGTM. I'll add idempotency + retry guidelines to the RFC. :+1:
Jordan: I'll include tracing and example OpenTelemetry maps.
Sara: I'll prototype a cost model showing cost multiplier for concurrency levels 1/4/8.
deploy-bot: Created INF-2345: "multi-tool-invocation-api: RFC + perf tests" assigned to Jordan, Matt, Sara.
Alisha: Thanks — we'll sync in FRIDAY planning to finalize scope.
Liz: +1, please add a short customer-facing FAQ about semantics for partial responses.
Matt: can we also include a small JS SDK example (streaming) in the RFC?
Alisha: yes — include JS and Python snippets.
Jordan: noting a future work item: cross-call KV cache hints (to co-locate repeated calls).
Sara: flagged for infra: quota impact and backend autoscaling if many customers enable high concurrency.
Alisha: closing for now. We'll reconvene after the RFC draft.
